marking_points.text: Applies Newton's second law to both particles ($T = 3a$ and $20 - T = 2a$) and adds to obtain $(3+2)a = 20$, finding acceleration $a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Substitutes $a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into either equation of motion to obtain tension $T = 12\text{ N}$.
Calculates friction $F = \mu R = 0.25 \times 40 = 10\text{ N}$, forms equations of motion $T - 10 = 4a$ and $60 - T = 6a$, and solves to find $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Substitutes $a = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to obtain tension $T = 30\text{ N}$.
Forms equations of motion $T - 2(10)\sin 30^\circ = 2a$ and $3(10) - T = 3a$, and solves for acceleration to find $a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculates the string tension $T = 30 - 3(4) = 18\text{ N}$.
Uses vector addition for two perpendicular tension forces of magnitude $15\text{ N}$ to find resultant force magnitude $R = \sqrt{15^2 + 15^2} = 15\sqrt{2}\approx 21.2\text{ N}$.
States that the direction of the force is at $45^\circ$ below the horizontal (towards the interior of the table edge corner).
Uses equation of motion for hanging mass $30 - T = 3(1.5)$ to obtain tension $T = 25.5\text{ N}$.
Uses $T - F = 5(1.5)$ to find friction $F = 18\text{ N}$, then uses $F = \mu R = \mu (50)$ to obtain $\mu = 0.36$.
Uses equation for hanging mass $40 - T = 4(2.5)$ to find tension $T = 30\text{ N}$.
Sets up equation along incline $T - M(10)\sin 30^\circ = M(2.5)$ and solves $30 = 7.5M$ to find $M = 4\text{ kg}$.
Sets up equations of motion for $A$ and $B$ ($T = 1.6a$ and $24 - T = 2.4a$), adding them to obtain $4.0a = 24$, giving $a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculates the tension $T = 1.6(6) = 9.6\text{ N}$.
Uses $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0, a = 6, s = 1.2$ to obtain $v^2 = 14.4$, giving $v = \sqrt{14.4} = 3.79\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or $\frac{6\sqrt{10}}{5}$).
Uses $v = u + at$ or $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to calculate time $t = \sqrt{\frac{2.4}{6}} = \sqrt{0.4} = 0.632\text{ s}$ (or $\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}\text{ s}$).
Resolves vertically on $A$ to find normal reaction $R = 30\text{ N}$, and computes $F = \mu R = 0.20 \times 30 = 6\text{ N}$.
Forms equations of motion $T - 6 = 3a$ and $20 - T = 2a$, and adds them to obtain $5a = 14$, giving acceleration $a = 2.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Substitutes $a = 2.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into an equation of motion to calculate tension $T = 20 - 2(2.8) = 14.4\text{ N}$.
Applies Pythagoras to the perpendicular string tensions on the pulley: $F_{\text{pulley}} = \sqrt{T^2 + T^2} = T\sqrt{2}$.
Calculates resultant force on pulley $F_{\text{pulley}} = 14.4\sqrt{2} \approx 20.4\text{ N}$ (or $\frac{72\sqrt{2}}{5}\text{ N}$).

Compares driving forces: $W_B = 30\text{ N}$ downwards versus component down plane $W_{A\parallel} = 20\sin 30^\circ = 10\text{ N}$, deducing $A$ accelerates up the plane, so friction acts down the plane.

Calculates $R = 20\cos 30^\circ = 17.32\text{ N}$, friction $F = 0.20 \times 17.32 = 3.464\text{ N}$, forms equations $T - 10 - 3.464 = 2a$ and $30 - T = 3a$, and solves to find $a = 3.31\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculates the tension $T = 30 - 3(3.307) = 20.1\text{ N}$.
Selects and applies constant acceleration formula $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0, s = 0.6$, and $a = 3.307\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculates speed $v = \sqrt{2(3.307)(0.6)} = \sqrt{3.969} = 1.99\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Applies Newton's second law to ascending particle $B$: $T - 1(10) = 1(1.2)$, finding tension $T = 11.2\text{ N}$.
Resolves forces on $A$ down the incline: $X + 4(10)\sin\theta - T = 4a$, substituting $\sin\theta = 0.6$ and $a = 1.2$.

Solves $X + 24 - 11.2 = 4(1.2)$ to find applied force $X = -8\text{ N}$, correctly interpreting that a force of magnitude $8\text{ N}$ acts down the plane if resisting or finding $X = -8\text{ N}$ implies it acts up the plane.
Uses $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0, a = 1.2$, and $t = 2.5$ to calculate distance traveled.
Calculates distance $s = \frac{1}{2}(1.2)(2.5)^2 = 3.75\text{ m}$.
Uses $v = u + at$ to find speed $v = 1.2 \times 2.5 = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Finds friction $F = 0.20 \times 30 = 6\text{ N}$ and sets up equations $T - 6 = 3a$ and $20 - T = 2a$.
Adds equations to show $5a = 14$, concluding acceleration $a = 2.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0, a = 2.8, s = 1.0$ to obtain $v = \sqrt{5.6} \approx 2.37\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or $\frac{2\sqrt{35}}{5}\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

Recognizes tension becomes zero ($T = 0$) after $B$ hits floor and applies Newton's second law to $A$: $-F = 3a_2 \implies -6 = 3a_2$, obtaining deceleration of magnitude $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (or $a_2 = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$).
Uses $0^2 = v^2 + 2a_2 s_2$ with $v^2 = 5.6$ and $a_2 = -2$ to calculate additional sliding distance $s_2 = \frac{5.6}{4} = 1.4\text{ m}$.
Calculates total distance moved by $A$: $s_{\text{total}} = s_1 + s_2 = 1.0 + 1.4 = 2.4\text{ m}$.
Calculates normal reaction $R = 1(10)\cos\alpha = 8\text{ N}$ and friction $F = \frac{1}{4}(8) = 2\text{ N}$ directed down the plane.

Sets up equations of motion along plane $T - 1(10)\sin\alpha - F = 1a \implies T - 6 - 2 = 1a$ and for hanging particle $2(10) - T = 2a$, adding them to obtain $12 = 3a$, showing $a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculates the string tension $T = 20 - 2(4) = 12\text{ N}$.
Uses $v^2 = 2as_1$ with $a = 4$ and $s_1 = 0.9$ to obtain $v^2 = 2(4)(0.9) = 7.2$, giving speed $v = \sqrt{7.2} = 2.68\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or $\frac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}$).
Applies Newton's second law to $A$ moving up plane with $T = 0$: $-1(10)\sin\alpha - F = 1a_2 \implies -6 - 2 = 1a_2$.
Finds deceleration of $A$ after the string becomes slack has magnitude $8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (or acceleration $a_2 = -8\text{ m s}^{-2}$).
Uses $0^2 = v^2 + 2a_2 s_2$ with $v^2 = 7.2$ and $a_2 = -8$ to find additional distance $s_2 = \frac{7.2}{16} = 0.45\text{ m}$.
Calculates total distance moved by $A$ from release: $s_{\text{total}} = 0.9 + 0.45 = 1.35\text{ m}$.
Calculates normal reaction $R = 20\text{ N}$ and friction $F = 0.25 \times 20 = 5\text{ N}$ on block $A$.
Applies Newton's second law to $A$: $T - 5 = 2(2.5)$ to find tension $T = 10\text{ N}$.
Applies Newton's second law to hanging mass $B$: $m(10) - T = m(2.5) \implies 10m - 10 = 2.5m$, solving $7.5m = 10$ to obtain $m = \frac{4}{3}\approx 1.33\text{ kg}$.
Computes the resultant force on the pulley from two perpendicular tension forces of $10\text{ N}$: $F_{\text{pulley}} = \sqrt{10^2 + 10^2} = 10\sqrt{2}\approx 14.1\text{ N}$.
Calculates speed of $A$ when $B$ hits floor: $v = \sqrt{4} = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Finds deceleration of $A$ when string is slack: $-5 = 2a_2 \implies a_2 = -2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and calculates additional distance $s_2 = \frac{0 - 2^2}{2(-2.5)} = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8\text{ m}$, concluding total distance $0.8 + 0.8 = 1.6\text{ m} < 3.5\text{ m}$ so $A$ does not reach the pulley.
Calculates time for Stage 1: $t_1 = \frac{v - u}{a_1} = \frac{2}{2.5} = 0.8\text{ s}$.
Calculates time for Stage 2: $t_2 = \frac{0 - 2}{-2.5} = 0.8\text{ s}$, giving total time $t_{\text{total}} = 0.8 + 0.8 = 1.6\text{ s}$.
